title: Path integral approach to the truncated Wigner approximation of driven-dissipative spins
authors: Viktoria Noel, Michael Fleischhauer, Igor Lesanovsky
abstract: Phase-space approaches such as the truncated Wigner approximation (TWA) provide an efficient semiclassical framework for performing approximate simulations of the dynamics of open quantum many-body systems outside the reach of exact numerical methods but beyond the mean-field level. For bosonic systems, TWA is known to be equivalent to a Keldysh path-integral formulation truncated at second order in the so-called quantum fluctuations. This semiclassical approach provides an alternative transparent route towards approximate stochastic equations of motion, which can be efficiently solved. Here we establish the corresponding path-integral formulation for interacting open spin-$1/2$ systems using the continuous $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ phase space. We show, in particular, that a consistent treatment of dissipation requires correctly mapping operator products onto the curved spin phase space, leading to stochastic equations that coincide with those obtained from the continuous TWA formulation and thus reproduce the exact dynamics of a single dissipative spin. Our results provide a unified field-theoretic foundation for the TWA to dissipative spin dynamics and offer a systematic starting point for extensions beyond the semiclassical approximation.
summary: This paper develops a rigorous path integral approach to apply the Truncated Wigner Approximation (TWA) to open, dissipative spin systems. By incorporating the necessary SU(2) star product into the Keldysh formulation, the authors overcome inconsistencies found in previous methods. The resulting framework provides a systematic and theoretically sound way to simulate complex quantum dynamics on curved phase spaces.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop a consistent path integral formulation for applying the Truncated Wigner Approximation (TWA) to open, driven-dissipative interacting spin systems.
main_result: The authors establish that incorporating the SU(2) star product into the path integral yields stochastic equations that correctly reproduce the exact dynamics of single dissipative spins, providing a unified field-theoretic foundation for TWA in this regime.
method: The work employs a Keldysh path-integral formulation on the continuous SU(2) phase space, adapting techniques from bosonic systems to handle spin operators via a non-commutative star product ($\star$).
model_or_system: The system under study is interacting open spin-1/2 systems, which can be realized in platforms like Rydberg atom arrays. The dynamics are governed by the Lindblad master equation.
key_observables: Expectation values of spin operators ($\langle\hat{O}angle$), represented as phase-space averages over the Wigner function or flattened symbol $\chi(\Omega)$.
important_parameters: The approximation is semiclassical, involving truncations related to quantum fluctuations and the order of corrections from the star product.
main_assumptions: The core assumption involves mapping operator products onto the curved spin phase space using a 'star product' ($\star$), which must be treated carefully as it generates $\mathcal{O}(1)$ corrections unlike in simpler bosonic cases.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the notes reference Figure 1 showing the Keldysh path integral contour and equations detailing the evolution step (Equation 20).
paper_structure: The paper builds by first defining the SU(2) phase space, then constructing the path integral for Lindblad evolution, focusing critically on deriving and implementing the necessary star product corrections to ensure consistency with known single-spin dynamics.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the limitations of applying semiclassical methods like TWA to spin systems where non-commutativity is crucial; correctly handling the star product is essential for obtaining physically accurate results beyond simple mean-field treatments.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. The Keldysh contour for Lindblad dynamics. (a): Evolution of the density matrix, ˆρ(t) = ˆU(t) ˆρ(t0) ˆU †(t): the initial state is propagated by ˆU(t) on one side and by ˆU †(t) on the other, so its evolution comprises two histories over the same time interval. (b): The two histories folded into the closed time contour: the system travels along the forward branch (+) and returns along the backward branch (−). The initial state ˆρ(t0) joins the two branches at the initial time, and the closure of the contour at the final time is implemented by computing the trace of ˆρ(tf). Dissipation couples the branches: in the term ˆLˆρˆL†, ˆL acts on the forward and ˆL† on the backward branch...

FIG. 2. Single-spin benchmark. Site magnetisation ⟨σz⟩ of a single driven-decaying spin: exact solution of the master equation (black), the stochastic equations of Table I (“TWA with star product”), and the variant with operator products replaced by ordinary multiplication of their symbols (“TWA w/o star product”) at detuning ∆= ΩR and on resonance, ∆= 0. On resonance all curves coincide, while at finite detun- ing the ordinary-product variant relaxes to a visibly displaced steady state.

FIG. 3. Accuracy of the TWA with and without the star-product corrections. The colour maps show the relative error of the steady-state, site-averaged magnetisation of an N = 10 Rydberg chain for the TWA with the jump operators evaluated with star-product corrections (left) and without it (right) for (a) resonant drive, ∆= 0 and (b) finite detuning, ∆= ΩR. All the heatmaps share the same colour scale. The middle panels show the time evolution of mz at the parameters marked on the maps by the triangle (ΩR/Γ = 4, V/Γ = 10, strongly interacting) and the square (ΩR/Γ = 8, V/Γ = 3, weakly interacting), compared with the exact quantum jump Monte Carlo solution (black).
